P1.evidence: Setter read-back was clean and named — 'Kim told me like few things about you, like roughly briefed me in, but to be honest, I'm kind of an old school guy. And I love to hear it from you directly.' The open question followed straight away: 'what is it that you really want to fix right now in terms of your fitness, health, and how can we actually help?' The frame was two parts of four, with nothing about what is in the way or what he needs, and no agreement was asked for.

P2.evidence: Six of nine covered and the facts are unusually complete because the prospect is forthcoming. Injuries were asked twice and properly — 'do you feel anywhere in your body, for example, lower back, hips, some stiffness, some aches?' then 'how about any injuries from the past, something that is popping up right now?' and 'Nothing that limits your movements?' Training was confirmed in detail including modality, frequency and incline. Diet was the strongest section, taken in four passes: overall, an example day, snacks specifically, and meal timing. Sleep and energy were both asked, and the sleep question is what surfaced the nocturia and the fact that a doctor has already cleared it. What was not asked: age, height and weight, all of which the prospect volunteered — 'I was 220 and I lost weight just through dieting to 190. And I'm six foot' and 'I'm 65' — and no health-conditions question at all, on a 65-year-old.

P3.evidence: The surface ladder ran better here than on any other call in the batch and the deep half did not run at all. 'What is it that you're trying to lose, to fix?' produced the belly and the flexibility; the rep then narrowed it correctly — 'Like the longevity type of thing?' — and the prospect chose flexibility as the priority. P3c was asked well: 'Do you think you will get into some other sport that you haven't tried before? What's been waiting on back burner?' which produced the most revealing answer of the call — 'if I was free, yes, I would definitely go and fight again, probably, you know, but not now' — and the reason, that he is his mother's 24-hour carer. The rep did not follow it. Nobody asked who else this impacts, nobody drove to identity or legacy, and there was no reflect-back. On a call with a 65-year-old whose own physical capacity is the only thing keeping an 85-year-old out of a care home, and who described his life as 'work home look after mom' with the programme as 'escapism', none of that was converted into a reason to buy.

P4.evidence: One good question and no follow-through. 'Why did you give up?' about eleven years of kung fu produced a genuine root cause in the prospect's own words: 'I do it for 10 years and then get bored.' The rep registered it — 'So you just got bored. Interesting. Interesting.' — and then dropped it entirely, which is a missed opportunity twice over, because it is both the pattern that will end this programme and the thing a six-month structure is best placed to answer. What have you tried was covered only incidentally through rapport about rugby, kung fu and Tai Chi. The one-thing-in-the-way question was never asked, and its answer was sitting in plain view: he is on call 24 hours a day for his mother.

P5.evidence: Not run. No two-year question, no willing-to-settle, no why-not, no line in the sand. This is the most consequential omission on the call. He is 65, sits thirteen hours a day, cannot touch his toes, and is the sole physical support for an unsteady 85-year-old — the cost of him losing function is not abstract, it is another person's independence, and he had already said his own mobility is the thing the gym is not fixing. None of it was raised.

P6.evidence: Something like a belief check ran before the price — 'let's talk about numbers first, just tell me like how do you feel in overall about this?' — and produced genuine enthusiasm: 'it's something I can do, it's something that I'm interested and I'm really excited... to do this is another like an escapism for me, it's great and I can put my all into it.' That is warmth rather than a commitment, and the scripted questions were not asked: nothing about whether he believes he can get there with the right structure and the right person in his corner, and nothing about whether there is any reason he would not go all in if he had everything he needed. The earlier fit check drew a lukewarm answer that was not pursued — 'Yeah, I'm just going to have to work with it. I'm going to have to work it in.'

P11.evidence: Payment was worked properly — three structures, a live financing application — and nothing was collected because the lender declined. The Trevor onboarding call was not mentioned once on this entire call, which is unusual for this rep and removes the strongest reason to move quickly. The agreement, welcome email, Skool link and questionnaire were all absent. The one step done well, and better than anywhere else in the batch, is the follow-up: a specific date and time negotiated around the prospect's staff being in the room and his mother's physiotherapy, then sent and confirmed live — 'I've got it on my calendar. I have it.'

objection_plays.detail: The diagnosis was right and the procedure was skipped. He isolated correctly and confirmed the nature of the objection — 'is it more that the money is tight right now with this?' and 'so it's just a matter of figuring out the logistical part of the investment' — which established that this was a cashflow problem, not a value problem, and the prospect confirmed it repeatedly. Then no financial picture was taken at all: no cash on hand, no monthly surplus, no cards, no limits, no investments. He went straight to three structures and then to a lender, which declined. Had the picture been taken, the two facts that actually govern this deal would have surfaced in two minutes — that the money runs through a business account his sister controls, and that he already holds an Affirm facility. Both emerged by accident at minute forty-four.

A textbook trigger and nothing ran. 'The financier, which is my sister, who runs the company accounts... I want to make sure she's on board' is the same structure as the spouse objection with a third party holding the money. None of the play was used: no money-aside belief question, no 'what obstacles might she raise', no 'is there any reason she would not want you healthier', no offer to bring her onto the call, and no deposit to create skin in the game. The rep booked a callback and let the deal leave the room. Compare the Hariharan call the day before, where the same rep ran this play almost completely and sent the prospect to talk to his wife live.

'Can you leave that with me?' was answered by pinning a specific date and time rather than agreeing to be contacted, which is the right instinct and is executed better here than on any other call in the batch — the rep worked around the prospect's staff being in the room and his mother's Tuesday physiotherapy, then confirmed the invite had landed. None of the scripted content ran, and given the objection was mechanical rather than psychological, that is defensible.

Age and flexibility risk, raised by the prospect himself and not addressed. A 65-year-old who has never stretched, cannot touch his toes and describes himself as stiff as a board said, unprompted, 'throwing a kettlebell around should stretch me out. And I might snap something or something. I don't know, but I want to try it.' The answer was 'Yeah, definitely. It's a different kind of movement.' There is no scripted move for a prospect voicing an injury concern about the core modality, and no clearance question exists anywhere in the process.

A non-client third party being brought into the training. The prospect stated twice that he will give his 85-year-old mother a kettlebell to use alongside him, and describes her as wobbly, unsure of herself, needing constant supervision and attending physiotherapy. There is no policy, no caution and no play — the rep answered 'That is so awesome man.' Whatever the commercial view, someone needs to decide what a rep says when a client proposes to teach ballistic lifting to a frail elderly relative.

Third-party financing declined live, for the second prospect in two days. 'Sorry, we're unable to offer you the payment plan at this time' arrived with no scripted response available; the rep asked for a screenshot and started re-quoting the six-month structure. The prospect rescued it himself by proposing his own financing. This needs a defined next move rather than improvisation.

notes: The best-qualified prospect in the batch on every criterion, blocked by a purely mechanical problem, and the two phases that would have secured him were the two that did not run — no consequence frame and no play on the sister who controls the money. Coach the sister as a spouse objection: ask what she would object to, ask whether there is any reason she would not want him healthier at 65, and offer to have her on the call. Second, take the financial picture before offering structures; the Affirm account and the company card both existed and neither was discovered until after a lender had already declined him.
